key_insight: Brief pretraining on random noise teaches neural nets to be uncertain before they see real data, which improves calibration and out-of-distribution detection without changing model architecture.
problem_solved: Overconfident neural networks that give unreliable probability estimates and fail to flag out-of-distribution inputs.
method: Briefly pretrain the model on random-noise inputs with a loss that encourages high-uncertainty (e.g., uniform/entropy-promoting targets).
Then fine-tune the same model on real labeled data as usual.
This simple two-stage training (noise → data) yields better-calibrated predictions and improved OOD identification.
impact: A low-cost, architecture-agnostic technique to make models more reliable and safer in deployment by reducing overconfidence and improving detection of unfamiliar inputs.

paper_title: Learning to be uncertain before learning from data
